speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. To better understand your neck swelling, have you noticed if it has been there for a long time, or did it appear suddenly? Also, have you experienced any pain, difficulty swallowing, or changes in your voice?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Colon Cancer to the Neck (Cervical Lymphadenopathy).

Based on your history of colon cancer and this new, painless, progressively enlarging mass on the back of your neck, I am highly concerned that this is a metastatic deposit. We need to immediately evaluate the mass and check for other signs of spread. REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_Ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_Abeldomen_Pelvis. REQUEST TEST: CEA_Level.
